title: What is a reranker? A plain-English guide to rerank models | reranker.uk
description: What is a reranker? A reranker (rerank model) re-scores retrieved candidates by relevance, usually as a second stage after fast retrieval. Learn how rerankers work, why they boost search and RAG quality, and when to use one.
og_title: What is a reranker? A plain-English guide
og_description: How rerank models re-score retrieved candidates to improve search and RAG quality.

  {"@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "FAQPage", "mainEntity": [{"@type": "Question", "name": "What is a reranker?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A reranker is a model that takes a query and a list of candidate documents and reorders them by how relevant each one actually is. It almost always runs as a second stage after a fast retriever has already narrowed a large corpus down to a shortlist."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Why is the order from vector search often wrong?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A vector retriever embeds the query and each document independently, with no chance for the two texts to interact, so a passage that merely shares vocabulary with the query can score as highly as one that genuinely answers it. The correct document is often in the top 50 candidates, just not near position 1."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "What is the two-stage retrieval pattern?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Stage one retrieves broadly and cheaply — vector search or BM25 over the whole corpus down to the top 50-100 candidates. Stage two reranks that shortlist with a cross-encoder, which is far more accurate but too slow to run over an entire corpus, then keeps only the top few."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "How does a cross-encoder reranker score relevance?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "It concatenates the query and a candidate document into one input and passes them through a transformer together, so every token of the query can attend to every token of the document. The output is a single relevance score, typically squashed to 0-1 with a sigmoid so it can be sorted or thresholded."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "When should I skip reranking?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Skip it when your retriever already returns near-perfect ordering for your domain, when you cannot afford the extra tens of milliseconds of latency for a second model call, or when your candidate set is already tiny and there is little left to reorder."}}]}
  </script>
